text: IMPARTIAL ANALYSIS OF MEASURE [TBD]

The Board of Trustees of the Jefferson Union High School District (District) proposes to adopt an education parcel tax to support various educational purposes, as outlined below. The District currently has in place a parcel tax of $58 per parcel (Measure Y) that this Measure would replace; if this Measure is approved, the District will cease to levy and collect the Measure Y parcel tax commencing with fiscal year 2027-28. This Measure, if approved by voters, would impose an annual tax of $98 per parcel for ten years, commencing with fiscal year 2027-28, and is estimated to raise approximately $3,400,000 annually.

The proposed parcel tax applies to any unit of land in the District that receives a separate tax bill from San Mateo County tax collection officials. All property that would otherwise be exempt from property taxes will also be exempt from the parcel tax. Any person 65 years of age or older who owns and occupies a parcel as a principal residence may apply to the District for an exemption from the tax. Property owners who have already qualified for a senior citizen exemption under the District's current parcel tax will automatically qualify for an exemption under this Measure.
The stated purposes of the proposed parcel tax are to:
• Support teachers and academic programs; • Expand and enhance career training and college preparedness classes; and Attract and retain qualified teachers, staff, and counselors at District schools.
The Measure provides that under no circumstances shall any proceeds of the parcel tax be used for administrators' salaries, benefits, or pensions.

The proceeds of the parcel tax will be placed in a special account. An annual report accounting for the amount of parcel tax funds collected and expended, and the status of any projects or programs funded by the tax, will be filed with the Board of Trustees. An independent Citizens' Oversight Committee will be appointed to review the expenditures of the parcel tax.

Current law forbids any decrease in State or Federal funding to the District because of the adoption of the parcel tax. If any such funding is reduced because of the parcel tax, the amount of the tax will be reduced annually as necessary to restore that funding.
A "yes" vote on this Measure would impose on property within the District an annual parcel tax of $98 for ten years, commencing with fiscal year 2027-28, for the purposes listed above.
A "no" vote on this Measure would not allow the parcel tax to be levied.
This Measure passes if at least two-thirds of those voting on the Measure vote "yes".
(500 word limit. 420 words)

text: Jefferson Union High School District Argument in Favor of Measure Our local public high schools--—Jefferson, Oceana, Shasta, Terra Nova, Thornton and Westmoor High Schools--—are vital to our community's prosperity and enhance the value of our homes and businesses. Your Yes vote of Measure _ will replace the District's existing parcel tax and provide local funding that cannot be taken by the State or Federal government and spent elsewhere. Measure comes with critical taxpayer protections including:

Transparency and Accountability: Public disclosure of all spending plus independent citizen oversight and third-party audits. Focused Spending: Funds may be used only for the specific purposes approved by voters---—supporting teachers, classrooms and academic programs. No funds may be spent on administrator salaries, pensions or benefits. Senior Citizen Exemption: Homeowners age 65 and over can apply for an exemption.
Within these strict limits, Measure supports:

• PEOPLE: Attracting and retaining qualified teachers, counselors and staff who provide consistent instruction, guidance and support. PATHWAYS: Expanding and enhancing college-preparation, career training and Career Technical Education classes that connect learning with real-world skills and opportunities. PROGRAMS: Protecting strong academic programs and classes that prepare students to succeed after graduation. • COMMUNITIES: High-quality schools increase the value of our homes and businesses. Vote YES on Measure _ to replace the current parcel tax in order to attract and retain qualified, dedicated teachers. Strong local high schools benefit the entire community and help protect local property values. Measure _ helps keep dedicated educators, and prepare graduates for college, careers and the future. Join parents, teachers, graduates, seniors and community leaders in voting YES on Measure

text: As a Pacifica resident and public school parent, I know firsthand how dedicated our teachers, principals, and staff are. They do remarkable work every single day. I strongly support public education, but continuously increasing property taxes without structural reform is not the right solution.

Local property owners are already carrying a heavy financial burden. Since 2012, you have approved $399.29 million in Jefferson Union High School bonds across Measures E (2012), J (2014), J (2020) and Z (2024). On typical tax bills, bond repayments alone add significant costs. It shows as "Jefferson UHSD Bond" costing me $1 , 144.23 this past year. Please check your own tax bill to see what you are already paying.

On top of bond debts, parcel taxes keep compounding. In 2024 Measure Z added a new $95 annual parcel tax. 2018 Measure Y currently costs $58 annually. There is also a Maintenance Assessment District tax that adds another $10 annually.

Measure is presented as a simple "replacement" for 2018 Measure Y, but it actually raises the tax from $58 to $98 per year - a tax hike on top of recent new taxes. Meanwhile, the ballot language is practically copy-pasted from 2018 and offers no new accountability standards, no structural changes, and no fresh ideas. It is just higher costs for local residents.
Taxpayers support our schools, but our community needs fiscal discipline and better leadership, not endless tax increases. Vote NO on Measure Encl

text: The opponent is right about two things: our dedicated teachers and staff do remarkable work every day, and nobody enjoys paying taxes. But he's wrong about Measure M. Here's Why:
Great schools require funding, and neither the State nor the Federal government provides enough to give our students the education they need for college and high- paying careers.

Measure M replaces the expiring 2018 parcel tax with an increase of less than a dollar a week per parcel. By law, these funds must stay local—the State cannot take them and spend them elsewhere. Keeping qualified teachers and staff in our classrooms, not cycling through new hires year after year, is what gives students consistency and results. Strong programs and steady instruction depend on the same thing: teachers who stay.

The opponent claims Measure M offers "no new accountability standards." This is also wrong. Even though State law does not require an independent Citizens' Oversight Committee for parcel taxes, Jefferson Union High School District's Board of Trustees voted to create one anyway. Together, the committee and annual public reporting will ensure full disclosure of all spending. Every dollar will go only to teachers, academic progrqms, and college and career preparation, never to administrator salaries, benefits, or pensions.
Our community shows up for our teachers, and our teachers show up for our students. Measure M protects that progress and keeps moving Jefferson Union High School District forward.
Vote Yes on Measure M!
